cards.title: 核心变化
cards.body: Claude 不只在默认 coding harness 内工作，而是能为研究、安全分析、agent teams、code review 等任务即时生成专用 harness。

cards.title: 解决问题
cards.body: 长任务容易出现 agentic laziness、self-preferential bias 和 goal drift，动态工作流通过隔离上下文和显式验证缓解这些失败模式。

cards.title: 使用边界
cards.body: Workflows 更适合复杂、高价值任务；普通 coding 任务未必需要额外 compute 或多个 reviewer。

rows.en: The default Claude Code harness is effective for coding, but it can break down over long-running, massively parallel, highly structured, or adversarial tasks.
rows.zh: 默认 Claude Code harness 对编码很有效，但在长期运行、大规模并行、高结构化或对抗式任务中可能失效。

rows.en: The article names three failure modes: agentic laziness, self-preferential bias, and goal drift.
rows.zh: 文章点名三个失败模式：代理式懒惰、自我偏好偏差，以及目标漂移。

rows.en: Static workflows need to work for all edge cases, so they are usually more generic.
rows.zh: 静态工作流要覆盖各种边界情况，因此通常更通用，也更不贴合具体任务。

rows.en: With Claude Opus 4.8 and dynamic workflows, Claude can write a custom harness tailor-made for the use case.
rows.zh: 借助 Claude Opus 4.8 和动态工作流，Claude 可以为用例编写量身定制的 harness。

rows.en: 04六个常见工作流模式
rows.zh: 本节围绕「04六个常见工作流模式」提炼来源要点。

rows.en: Use cases include migrations and refactors, deep research, deep verification, sorting, memory and rule adherence, root-cause investigation, triage at scale, exploration and taste, evals, and model routing.
rows.zh: 典型用例包括迁移与重构、深度研究、深度验证、排序、记忆与规则遵循、根因调查、大规模分诊、探索与品味、评估，以及模型路由。

rows.en: Workflows are a helpful new way to extend Claude Code, but they are not needed for every task.
rows.zh: Workflows 是扩展 Claude Code 的新方式，但不是每个任务都需要它。

rows.en: The practical decision is whether a task benefits from isolated context, parallel exploration, adversarial verification, or repeated loops.
rows.zh: 真正的判断标准是：这个任务是否受益于隔离上下文、并行探索、对抗式验证或循环执行。

rows.en: Last week, we released [dynamic workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows) in Claude Code. Claude can now write its own [harness](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/glossary#agentic-harness) on the fly, custom-built for the task at hand.
rows.zh: 上周，我们在 Claude Code 中发布了动态工作流。Claude 现在可以即时编写自己的 harness，并为手头的任务量身定制。
rows.html: Last week, we released dynamic workflows in Claude Code. Claude can now write its own harness on the fly, custom-built for the task at hand.
rows.zhHtml: 上周，我们在 Claude Code 中发布了动态工作流。Claude 现在可以即时编写自己的 harness，并为手头的任务量身定制。

rows.en: While the default Claude Code harness is built for coding, it is also useful for many other types of tasks because, as it turns out, many tasks resemble coding tasks. But there are certain classes of tasks where we have had to build custom harnesses on top of Claude Code to achieve peak performance such as [Research](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11088861-using-research-on-claude), [security analysis](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11932705-automated-security-reviews-in-claude-code), [agent teams](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams), or [Code Review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review).
rows.zh: 虽然默认的 Claude Code harness 是为编码而构建的，但它对许多其他类型的任务也很有用，因为事实证明，许多任务都类似编码任务。不过，对于研究、安全分析、agent teams 或代码审查等某些类别的任务，我们不得不在 Claude Code 之上构建自定义 harness，才能达到最佳性能。

But there are certain classes of tasks where we have had to build custom harnesses on top of Claude Code to achieve peak performance such as Research, security analysis, agent teams, or Code Review.

rows.en: Workflows allow you to dynamically create harnesses built on top of Claude Code that enable Claude to solve all of those problems more natively. You can also share and reuse these workflows with others.
rows.zh: 工作流让你能够动态创建构建在 Claude Code 之上的 harness，使 Claude 能够更自然地解决所有这些问题。你也可以与他人分享并复用这些工作流。

rows.en: In this article, I’ll cover my initial workflows experiences and learnings so you can best take full advantage. Keep in mind, best practices are still developing: dynamic workflows often use more tokens and are best suited for complex, high value tasks.

rows.en:
Before diving into the technical details, I’d like to start with several example prompts to get you thinking about the possibilities with workflows:

> "This test fails maybe 1 in 50 runs. Set up a workflow to reproduce it. Form competing theories about the race, and don't stop until one theory survives the evidence."

> "Using a workflow, go through my last 50 sessions and mine them for corrections I keep making and turn the recurring ones into `CLAUDE.md` rules"

> "Use a workflow to dig through #incidents in Slack for the past six months and find recurring root causes where nobody has filed a ticket."

> "Take my business plan and run a workflow where different agents tear it apart from an investor's, a customer's, and a competitor's perspective."
rows.zh:
在深入技术细节之前，我想先从几个示例 prompt 开始，让你思考工作流可能带来的可能性：

“这个测试大约每运行 50 次会失败 1 次。建立一个工作流来复现它。针对这个竞态形成多个相互竞争的理论，并且在某个理论经受住证据检验之前不要停止。”

“使用一个工作流，浏览我最近 50 个会话，挖掘其中我反复做出的修正，并把反复出现的修正转成 CLAUDE.md 规则。”

“使用一个工作流，深挖过去六个月 Slack 中的 #incidents，找出那些反复出现但没人提交工单的根因。”

“拿我的商业计划运行一个工作流，让不同 agent 分别从投资者、客户和竞争对手的视角对它进行严厉审视。”

rows.en:
It’s particularly useful to know that dynamic workflows can decide which models an agent uses and whether subagents are run in their own worktree, allowing Claude to choose the intelligence level and isolation needed.

If a workflow is interrupted, for example by user action or quitting the terminal, resuming the session will allow the workflow to pick up where it left off.
rows.zh:
尤其有用的一点是，动态工作流可以决定 agent 使用哪些模型，以及子代理是否在各自的 worktree 中运行，从而让 Claude 选择所需的智能水平和隔离程度。

如果工作流被中断，例如由于用户操作或退出终端而中断，恢复会话后，工作流将能够从中断处继续。

rows.en:
When you ask the default Claude Code harness to do a task, it needs to both plan and execute in the same context window. For many coding tasks, this is highly effective, but it can break down over long-running, massively parallel, highly structured and/or adversarial tasks.

This is because the longer Claude works on a complex task in a single context window, the more it becomes susceptible to a few specific failure modes:
rows.zh:
当你让默认的 Claude Code harness 执行任务时，它需要在同一个上下文窗口中同时规划和执行。对许多编码任务来说，这非常有效，但在长时间运行、大规模并行、高度结构化和/或对抗式任务中，它可能会失效。

这是因为 Claude 在单个上下文窗口中处理复杂任务的时间越长，就越容易受到几种特定失败模式的影响：

这是因为 Claude 在单个上下文窗口中处理复杂任务的时间越长，就越容易受到几种特定失败模式的影响：

rows.en:
- **Agentic laziness** refers to when Claude stops before finishing a particularly complex, multi-part task and declares the job done after partial progress, for example addressing 35 of the 50 items in a security review.
- **Self-preferential bias** refers to Claude’s tendency to prefer its own results or findings, especially when asked to verify or judge them against a rubric.
- **Goal drift** refers to the gradual loss of fidelity to the original objective across many turns, especially after compaction. Each summarization step is lossy, and details like edge-case requirements or "don't do X" constraints can get lost.
rows.zh: Agentic laziness 指 Claude 在完成某个特别复杂的多部分任务之前就停下来，并在取得部分进展后宣称任务已完成，例如在安全审查中只处理了 50 项中的 35 项。Self-preferential bias 指 Claude 倾向于偏好自己的结果或发现，尤其是在被要求依据评分标准验证或评判这些结果时。Goal drift 指经过许多轮对话后，尤其是在压缩之后，对原始目标的忠实度逐渐降低。每一步总结都会丢失信息，边界情况要求或“不要做 X”之类的约束可能会丢失。

Each summarization step is lossy, and details like edge-case requirements or "don't do X" constraints can get lost.

rows.en: Creating a workflow helps combat these by orchestrating separate Claude subagents with their own context windows and focused, isolated goals.

groups.group: Helpful patterns when using dynamic workflows

rows.en:
You can start using dynamic workflows just by asking Claude to make one, or by using the trigger word `ultracode` to ensure that Claude Code creates a workflow.

But building a mental model for how dynamic workflows work will help you understand when to use them and how you might nudge Claude via prompts.

There are a few common patterns that Claude might use and compose together when building workflows:

不过，建立动态工作流如何运作的心智模型，会帮助你理解什么时候使用它们，以及如何通过 prompt 引导 Claude。

rows.alt: Common workflow patterns can be composed into a task-specific harness.

rows.en: Use a classifier agent to decide on the type of task, and then route to different agents or behavior based on the task. Or, use a classifier at the end to determine output.
rows.zh: 使用分类器 agent 判断任务类型，然后根据任务将其路由到不同的 agent 或行为。或者，在末尾使用分类器来确定输出。
rows.html: Use a classifier agent to decide on the type of task, and then route to different agents or behavior based on the task. Or, use a classifier at the end to determine output.
rows.zhHtml: 使用分类器 agent 判断任务类型，然后根据任务将其路由到不同的 agent 或行为。或者，在末尾使用分类器来确定输出。

rows.en:
Split up a task into many smaller steps, run an agent on each step and then synthesize those results. This is particularly useful for when there are a large number of smaller steps, or when each step benefits from its own clean context window so they don't interfere or cross-contaminate. The synthesize step is a barrier: it waits for all the fan-out agents, then merges their structured outputs into one result.

For each spawned agent, run a separate spawned agent to adversarially verify its output against a rubric or criteria.
rows.zh:
把一个任务拆成许多更小的步骤，在每个步骤上运行一个 agent，然后综合这些结果。当存在大量小步骤时，或者每个步骤都能从自身干净的上下文窗口中受益、从而避免相互干扰或交叉污染时，这尤其有用。综合步骤是一个屏障：它等待所有扇出 agent 完成，然后把它们的结构化输出合并成一个结果。

对于每个被启动的 agent，再运行一个单独启动的 agent，依据评分标准或准则对其输出进行对抗式验证。

rows.en: Instead of dividing the work, have agents compete on it. Spawn N agents that each attempt the same task using different approaches. Prompts or models then judge the results in a pairwise fashion using a judging agent until you have a winner.
rows.zh: 不要拆分工作，而是让 agent 围绕它展开竞争。启动 N 个 agent，让它们分别用不同方法尝试同一任务。随后由 prompt 或模型通过一个评判 agent 以两两比较的方式评判结果，直到选出胜者。

rows.en: The key is to break down the task into a series of steps that need to be operated on, for example callsites, failing tests, modules, and related units. Spin off a subagent for every fix in a worktree to make the fix, then have another agent adversarially review, and merge them. Consider telling the agent not to use resource intensive commands so that you can maximally parallelize without running out of resources on your machine.
rows.zh: 关键是把任务拆解成一系列需要处理的步骤，例如调用点、失败的测试、模块和相关单元。为每个修复在一个 worktree 中派生一个子代理来完成修复，然后让另一个 agent 进行对抗式审查，并合并它们。可以考虑告诉 agent 不要使用资源密集型命令，这样你就能最大程度并行化，而不会耗尽机器资源。

rows.en: If you have a report where you want to check and source every factual claim that it references, you may want to generate a workflow which has one agent identify all of the factual claims and then spin off a subagent to check each one in detail. rows.en: You may have a list of items that you want to sort by some qualitative measurement that you believe Claude Code is good at evaluating, for example support tickets sorted by severity of the bug. But if you try to sort 1000+ rows in one prompt, quality degrades and it won't fit in context. Instead run a tournament, a pipeline of pairwise-comparison agents, or bucket-rank in parallel then merge. Comparative judgment is more reliable than absolute scoring. Each comparison is its own agent, so the deterministic loop holds the bracket and only the running order stays in context.
rows.zh: 你可能有一组条目，希望按照某种你认为 Claude Code 擅长评估的定性标准来排序，例如按 bug 严重程度排序的支持工单。但如果你试图在一个 prompt 中排序 1000 多行，质量会下降，而且无法放入上下文。相反，可以运行锦标赛、一条两两比较 agent 的流水线，或并行分桶排序后再合并。相对比较判断比绝对打分更可靠。每次比较都是自己的 agent，因此确定性的循环负责保存对阵表，只有运行顺序留在上下文中。

rows.en: If you have a particular set of rules that you find Claude misses or struggles with, even when put into the `CLAUDE.md` files, create a workflow with a list of rules that must be checked by verifier agents, one verifier per rule. Creating a skeptic persona subagent to review the rules to make sure they are in line will help avoid too many false positives.
rows.zh: 如果你有一组特定规则，发现 Claude 即使在放入 CLAUDE.md 文件后仍会遗漏或难以遵守，可以创建一个工作流，列出必须由验证 agent 检查的规则，每条规则对应一个验证 agent。创建一个怀疑者人格的子代理来审查这些规则是否合理，有助于避免过多误报。

rows.en: The reverse direction works too: mine your recent sessions and code review comments for corrections you keep making, cluster them with parallel agents, adversarially verify each candidate, and then distill the survivors back into a `CLAUDE.md`.
rows.zh: 反向流程也同样可行：挖掘你最近的会话和代码审查评论，找出你反复做出的修正，用并行 agent 对它们聚类，对每个候选项进行对抗式验证，然后把保留下来的内容提炼回 CLAUDE.md。

rows.alt: Memory and rule adherence workflows can mine recurring corrections and distill them into durable rules.

rows.en: Debugging works best when you come up with several independent hypotheses and test them, but if you’re only using one context window, Claude can run into self-preferential bias.
rows.zh: 调试在提出多个独立假设并测试它们时效果最好；但如果你只使用一个上下文窗口，Claude 可能会陷入自我偏好偏差。

rows.en:
A workflow can structurally prevent this by spinning up agents to generate hypotheses from disjoint evidence. For example, separate agents for logs, files, and data. Each hypothesis can then face a panel of verifiers and refuters.

This isn't just for code. Workflows can be used for sales, data engineering, or any post-mortem exercise.

Every team has a support queue, bug reports, or some other backlog that cannot be fully processed by humans.
rows.zh:
工作流可以通过启动 agent 从互不重叠的证据中生成假设，在结构上防止这种情况。例如，为日志、文件和数据分别设置 agent。随后，每个假设都可以面对一组验证者和反驳者。

这不只适用于代码。工作流可以用于销售、数据工程，或任何事后复盘练习。

每个团队都有支持队列、bug 报告，或其他无法由人工完全处理的积压事项。

rows.en:
A useful pattern for triage workflows is quarantine. This involves barring the agents that read untrusted public content from taking high-privilege actions, which are instead done by the agents in charge of acting on the information.

Pair triage workflows with `/loop` to have Claude do this continuously.

将分诊工作流与 /loop 配对，可以让 Claude 持续执行此类工作。

groups.group: When not to use dynamic workflows

rows.en: Workflows are new. While there are many use cases where it will create outsized results, they are not needed for every task and may end up using significantly more tokens.
rows.zh: 工作流是新东西。虽然有许多用例会产生超出比例的效果，但它们并不是每个任务都需要的，而且最终可能会使用多得多的 token。

rows.en: It’s best to use workflows creatively to push Claude Code in ways that you haven’t previously. For regular coding tasks, try and ask yourself: does it really need more compute? For example, most traditional coding tasks do not need a panel of 5 reviewers.

rows.en:
You can set explicit token usage budgets for dynamic workflows to limit how many tokens a task uses. You can prompt it with a budget like "use 10k tokens," which will set the cap.

You can save workflows by pressing "s" in the workflow menu. You can check these into `~/.claude/workflows` or distribute them via a skill.

rows.en: To share them via a skill, put your JavaScript workflow files in the skill folder and reference them in the `SKILL.md`. To allow for more flexibility, you may want to prompt Claude to think of the workflows in the skill as a template instead of a script that needs to be run verbatim.

groups.group: A new starting point for discovery

rows.en:
Workflows are a helpful new way to extend Claude Code. I encourage you to think of them as a starting point to explore new ways to use Claude to help accomplish your tasks. There is still much to discover in how to use them best.

This article was written by Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria, members of technical staff at Anthropic working on Claude Code.
